elements.element: Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation.
elements.evidence: Section 8.2 as rendered still binds Ono: "neither Ono or its Affiliates ... shall Commercialize in the Ono Territory ... [any] Competing Product", plus a post-termination tail. The redline narrows rather than deletes the covenant, so the preferred no-exclusivity position is not achieved.

elements.element: Exclusivity is limited to a defined product category.
elements.evidence: Retained language defines the restricted category by reference to specified active pharmaceutical ingredient classes ((i) ... other than Binimetinib; (ii) ... other than Encorafenib) and labels them "(each a "Competing Product")", and the restriction is further confined to the Ono Territory (Japan/Korea). No edit was needed for this element.

elements.element: Exclusivity lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Added sentence: "The obligations of Ono and its Affiliates under this Section 8.2 shall in no event continue beyond the twelve (12) month anniversary of the Effective Date". The "in no event" override reaches all Ono obligations in 8.2, including the retained post-termination tail to the "[ * ] anniversary of the date such termination takes effect", so the cap is not exceeded. The retained tail sentence is left standing but is subordinated by the express override rather than contradicting it.

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet service levels.
elements.evidence: The added exit reads "shall terminate automatically if Array fails to meet the service levels or delivery dates under any supply agreement between the Parties." The trigger is anchored solely to a "supply agreement between the Parties" that is not a defined term in the supplied text and that Article IX appears only to contemplate; there is no shown source of "service levels". If no such separate supply agreement is executed (or it contains no service levels), the automatic exit never fires, making the trigger potentially illusory.

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet delivery dates.
elements.evidence: Same single added trigger; the delivery-date exit likewise depends on "any supply agreement between the Parties" rather than on Array's supply obligations under Article IX of this Agreement. Because that instrument is undefined/contingent on the face of the redline, the automatic termination on missed delivery dates cannot be confirmed to operate.

reasons: Preferred level is not reached and was not attempted: the Ono-side non-compete in Section 8.2 survives, so only the fallback is in play.

Fallback is incomplete because both performance-exit elements hang on an external, undefined trigger. Repair in operative language: replace "under any supply agreement between the Parties" with a self-executing anchor, e.g. "if Array fails to meet its supply obligations under Article IX of this Agreement (including any agreed delivery dates or service levels) or under any supply agreement entered into between the Parties", and state the failure standard (e.g. material failure to deliver conforming Product by an agreed delivery date, uncured for [30] days).

Product-category and 12-month elements are satisfied on the operative text: the retained "Competing Product" definition supplies the category, and the added "in no event continue beyond the twelve (12) month anniversary of the Effective Date" caps every Ono obligation in Section 8.2, including the post-termination tail.

Minimality holds: Array's reciprocal covenant and the Array-Commercializes royalty-termination mechanic are untouched, no unrelated wording is deleted, and the only collateral edit ("in breach of this Section 8.2" in Array's termination trigger) is the conforming change required to prevent Array terminating for conduct the new cap permits.

Intent is preserved: Ono keeps the benefit of Array's mirror covenant, cross-references relied on by Article XIII/XIV remain intact, and the retained tail sentence is expressly overridden rather than left in conflict. Consider deleting the now-inoperative tail sentence in a later pass for clarity, but that is not required for completeness.

Optional tightening (not required by the checklist): confirm Article IX/Section 9.4(a) continues to leave Ono free to Manufacture or engage a Subcontractor, so no second exclusivity arises by operation of the supply provisions.
